title: Opt-in remote Linux host target for ./lab (follow-up to epic #35)
objective: Add an explicit remote-target mode so ./lab can run the agent container on an existing Linux host over SSH, while local QEMU/KVM stays the default. This is deliberately outside epic #35's completion criteria: it is the second topology the owner asked to track, not the one being implemented now.

acceptance_criteria.text: Local QEMU/KVM remains the default: a plain ./lab <dir> never touches a remote host, and remote mode requires an explicit --vm-target remote (or equivalent config) plus a visible confirmation.
Connection details (host, user, port, key path) come from gitignored config/env; no key or credential is copied into the workspace, image or ticket, and git status --short is clean after a session.
The same host-side check_workspace() guards run before anything is sent to the remote host: /, $HOME, the lab repo without --unsafe-recurse, and credential directories are refused and never exported.

Workspace transport is explicit (sshfs preferred, rsync fallback), exports only the selected directory, and documents latency, conflict and copy-back behaviour; the remote host sees no other local path.

The remote host runs the agent container with the same hardening and can run the workspace compose dependencies; no host ports are published, .mester-egress is enforced, and teardown removes labelled containers, networks, volumes and the transport mount.
./lab remote status/down is idempotent and a failed connection gives an actionable error; there is no silent fallback that starts the agent on the local host.
SECURITY.md and README state that remote mode shares the target host Docker daemon and is weaker isolation than the local VM, and recommend the local VM for untrusted code.
Tests cover local-default regression, remote provisioning, refused paths, transport round-trip, no-published-ports, egress deny, teardown residue and docs review.

needed: local default regression (remote mode not entered)
remote provisioning against a clean Linux host
no-published-ports check on the remote host
docs review of the weaker-isolation warning

comments.author: cli
comments.body: Created 2026-10-26 as the follow-up the owner asked for when choosing local QEMU/KVM: option 1 is the implementation target for epic #35, and this ticket tracks option 2 (local default + remote override) separately. It is intentionally NOT a child of #35, so it does not block the epic.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: Depends on #40 (control channel/transport decision) and #41 (VM lifecycle commands) so the remote target reuses the same path guards, labels, teardown and egress contract instead of growing a second harness. The engine stores dependencies but does not yet gate status transitions on them; that is #39.
